items.title: HyprBSD Provides Wayland-Based Desktop Built Atop FreeBSD, Complete With Steam Gaming
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>While FreeBSD has been working to improve its desktop and laptop experience, that work isn't yet shipping in released form for the OS installer and other ongoing efforts. Now there's a new desktop FreeBSD distribution on the scene with HyprBSD providing a Wayland-based desktop experience and with the Linux binary compatibility layer even an easy route to gaming with Steam...</article>

items.title: Kmorph Aims To Provide Rebootless Linux Kernel Crash Recovery
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Kmorph aims to provide reboot-less kernel crash recovery for Linux systems and can yield as little as ~2 second downtime for recovering the Nginx web server or other important services in the case of a kernel crash...</article>

items.title: KDE Plasma 6.9 Will Stop Leaking Memory When Right Clicking Files/Folders On Desktop
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>With Plasma 6.8 stable approaching one month old, KDE developers continue ramping up work toward Plasma 6.9. Here is some of the interesting work they've been up to so far in November...</article>

items.title: Vulkan 1.4.368 Released With New Extensions From Valve & NVIDIA
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Vulkan 1.4.368 is out as the newest weekly spec update for this high performance graphics and compute API...</article>

items.title: Microsoft's Azure Linux 3.0.2022 Ships With More Than 470 Security Fixes
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Microsoft released Azure Linux 3.0.2022 on Friday night as the newest version of their in-house Linux distribution. Given the rampant AI/LLM-fueled bug reporting and security research, Azure Linux 3.0.2022 ends up incorporating more than 470 security fixes for different CVEs across the many open-source projects making up Azure Linux...</article>

items.title: Asahi Linux Makes Progress On Gaming, More Apple Silicon Upstreaming
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Given the recent Linux 7.3 upstream kernel release, the Asahi Linux project published a new status report to outline recent code they have upstreamed to the mainline kernel as well as other efforts taking shape in their downstream codebase...</article>

items.title: FreeBSD 15.2 Beta 1 Allows Experimental Cross-Building Of Base Packages On Linux/macOS
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>FreeBSD 15.2 Beta 1 is out today as the release dance kicks off in working toward the next installment of FreeBSD 15...</article>

items.title: ReactOS Lands Initial USB3 Driver Support
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>After years of work, ReactOS as the "open-source Windows" operating system striving for Windows program and driver compatibility now has an initial USB 3.0 driver stack in place...</article>

items.title: A RISC-V Based TEE With AMD Zen 6 CPUs
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>An interesting technical detail I noticed today from the latest AMD Linux activity is that Zen 6 processors apparently are featuring a RISC-V based Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) where in the past it was an ARM-based core...</article>

items.title: Linux 7.4-rc2 Change Yields As Much As 162x Improvement For FAT32
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>In addition to a FAT32 optimization yielding as much as a 265x improvement that was merged for the Linux 7.4 cycle and separately another big FAT32 improvement expected for Linux 7.5, merged this week as part of the non-MM fixes for Linux 7.4-rc2 was another big FAT32 performance optimization...</article>

items.title: Arch Linux vs. CachyOS vs. Omarchy 4.5 Performance Benchmarks
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>With CachyOS recently having rolled out its Linux 7.3 based kernel and various other improvements plus with Omarchy 4.5 having been released this week, this article provides a look at how CachyOS and Omarchy are competing on the performance front relative to upstream Arch Linux.</article>

items.title: Linux x86 32-bit Patches Clean Old Kernel Code After Recently Removing Vintage CPUs
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>With the Linux kernel having phased out i486 CPU support and dropping old AMD Elan SoC code along with removing other obsolete and stagnate 32-bit x86 hardware support, some x86 32-bit clean-ups are proceeding along with being able to make the kernel depend unconditionally now on some features...</article>

items.title: FEX Awaits The Linux Kernel To Align With Windows & macOS On ARM Register Usage
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>FEX 2611 is out for running Linux (and Wine) x86/x86_64 games/applications on AArch64 Linux. FEX 2611 brings JIT improvements while also waiting for the Linux kernel to align with the AArch64 specification and Windows on ARM and macOS Apple Silicon behavior around a particular register's usage...</article>

items.title: Ubuntu Moving Ahead With Plans For Splitting Up Linux-Firmware, HWE Option
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>A few months back were discussions of a Linux firmware HWE package for Ubuntu to carry updated firmware blobs under the hardware enablement (HWE) umbrella. Plus also splitting up the monolithic linux-firmware package for easing of firmware updates. Those plans didn't materialize in time for the official Ubuntu 26.10 release but are now being pursued for Ubuntu 27.04 and may then be SRU'ed into Ubuntu 26.10 and potentially Ubuntu 26.04 LTS...</article>

items.title: Linux Developers Look To Drop RT_GROUP_SCHED As It's "Broken Beyond Repair"
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Linux kernel developers are looking at dropping the RT_GROUP_SCHED feature that is used for group scheduling of real-time tasks using cgroups...</article>

items.title: Sound Subsystem Seeing Lots Of Fixes & Laptop/Device Quirks For Linux 7.4-rc2
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>The sound subsystem is seeing a "unsurprisingly high amount" fixes and device workarounds/quirks for this weekend's Linux 7.4-rc2 kernel release...</article>

items.title: OpenCV 5.1 Brings More AVX-512 Optimizations, Other Improvements
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>OpenCV 5.0 debuted back in June with a rewritten DNN engine and many other exciting improvements for this widely-used computer vision (CV) library. Out today is OpenCV 5.1 with tons of fixes and other incremental improvements to this important code...</article>

items.title: AMDGPU Driver Seeing HDMI 2.2 FRL Fixes For Linux 7.4
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>With Linux 7.4 the AMDGPU driver enables HDMI 2.1 FRL functionality by default for driving higher refresh rate and higher resolution displays. That default enabling comes as HDMI FreeSync/VRR and ALLM features are also in place for Linux 7.4. Now coming by way of fixes for Linux 7.4 is also improving the Fixed Rate Link support with the newer HDMI 2.2 specification...</article>

items.title: Linux 7.4's Build Time Performance From Optimizations But Also Larger Codebase
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>With Linux 7.4 the patches to speed-up the kernel build process began to land. This is the work that's yielded extremely fast incremental builds and noop builds. The patch series in full is also allowing kernel build times approaching just ten seconds with enough CPU cores. In today's article is a look at the Linux 7.3 vs. 7.4-rc1 build time performance on the Framework Laptop 13 Pro powered by Intel Panther Lake...</article>

items.title: Linux's RAID6 Check Tool Sees 3x Performance Via Batching
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>For those that use Linux's raid6check command for checking/repairing an MD RAID6 software RAID array's device for errors, newly-merged code is showing up to a 3x performance improvement...</article>

items.title: Servo Browser Engine Continues Broadening Web Compatibility, New Features
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>The Servo open-source browser engine project is finally out with their status report highlighting the improvements made back in September. There is expanded web compatibility, new HTML and JavaScript features, WebGL2 improvements, and continued work on expanding the embed capabilities of this engine...</article>

items.title: Zlib 1.4 Released With More Than One Dozen Security Fixes
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Zlib 1.4 is now available for this widely-used compression library. In these AI times, Zlib 1.4 ships with more than a dozen security fixes...</article>

items.title: Linux Kernel Patches Posted For Review In Enabling Apple AirDrop Support
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>A set of Linux kernel patches have been posted for review with a hope of reaching the mainline kernel to provide Apple AirDrop support for Macs equipped with the T2 chip...</article>

items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Mir 2.31 is now available as the latest feature release for this Canonical/Ubuntu solution for providing C++ libraries to build Wayland-based shells...</article>

items.title: Linux'x New Core MM Tree Ready With Numerous Fixes For "Nasty Long-Standing Bugs"
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>New to the Linux 7.4 kernel cycle is the Core MM tree as the route for herding some of the core memory management Linux kernel patches to the mainline kernel rather than it all going through Andrew Morton's "MM" tree.  As the second pull request from this new kernel tree, a number of fixes were sent out today to address "nasty long-standing bugs" within the kernel...</article>

items.title: Mesa Merges A Common Vulkan Layer For Working Around Cross-Driver Game Bugs
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Merged to Mesa 27.0-devel is a new common Vulkan layer within Mesa's Vulkan Runtime for being able to carry common game/engine/app workarounds that affect multiple drivers...</article>

items.title: AMD-Backed Lemonade Local AI Server Ships Redesigned Desktop App & Web UI
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>The AMD-backed Lemonade local AI server shipped its version 2026.45.3 update on Wednesday that introduces a completely redesigned desktop app and web UI...</article>

items.author: Michael Larabel

items.title: OpenAI Finds 948 Local Privilege Escalation Bugs In The Linux Kernel
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>OpenAI published a blog post outlining their work on autonomous vulnerability discovery. To showcase their AI potential, they found 948 valid local privilege escalation vulnerabilities within the Linux kernel...</article>

items.title: Linux 7.4 Showing Few Performance Gains With Initial Benchmarks On AMD Ryzen Threadripper
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>In the first round of benchmarking the in-development Linux 7.4 kernel there are some performance improvements -- and some small regressions -- worth noting over the current Linux 7.3 stable kernel. This first round of Linux 7.4 kernel benchmarking was on a System76 Thelio Major workstation with AMD Ryzen Threadripper 9980X.</article>
